::: {#exr-miller-int-polynomial}
#### Definite integral of a polynomial

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.31.

Evaluate the integral:

$$\int_0^1 (x^4 + x^2 + 1)\,dx$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-int-polynomial}
Integrate term by term using the power rule for integration:

$$\ba
\int_0^1 (x^4 + x^2 + 1)\,dx &= \sb{\frac{x^5}{5} + \frac{x^3}{3} + x}_0^1
\\
&= \paren{\frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{3} + 1} - 0 \\
&= \frac{3 + 5 + 15}{15} \\
&= \frac{23}{15}
\ea$$
:::
